name: Quincy
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Quincy, MA 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in Quincy, MA: Santa by helicopter at Pageant Field, the Hancock Street parade, a free skating rink and Santa at Kilroy Square.
lede: Quincy packs its Christmas into Thanksgiving weekend: a tree lighting in Quincy Center, Santa landing by helicopter at Pageant Field and one of the South Shore's longest running Christmas parades on Hancock Street.
celebrates: Quincy starts the season on the Friday after Thanksgiving with a tree lighting in Quincy Center. The next day Santa and his elves arrive by helicopter at Pageant Field, where families meet holiday characters while they wait for the landing. On Sunday the City of Quincy holds its Christmas Parade, with floats, marching bands and costumed characters on Hancock Street and Santa riding at the end. After the parade weekend the city opens a free outdoor skating rink in Quincy Center, and the Quincy Chamber of Commerce runs the Kilroy Square Holiday Market for two weekends, with local makers in a heated tent and visits with Santa.
lastyear: In 2025 Santa arrived by helicopter at Pageant Field on Saturday, November 29, and The Patriot Ledger shared photos of the landing. The next day, Sunday, November 30, the City of Quincy held its 72nd Christmas Parade, starting at noon at Hancock Street and Walter J. Hannon Parkway and heading up Hancock Street to North Quincy High School. Discover Quincy promised floats, marching bands and costumed characters, with Santa anchoring the parade before heading home to the North Pole.
facts: Quincy and Milton share the title of home of America's first railroad. The Granite Railway opened on October 7, 1826, carrying granite from the quarries in West Quincy through East Milton to the Neponset River, where it was shipped to Charlestown for the Bunker Hill Monument. Horses pulled cars that railway pioneer Gridley Bryant designed to carry stone. The Quincy Christmas Parade reached its 72nd year in 2025, and the city counts the 2026 parade as its 73rd.
trains: Quincy Center station, at 175 Thomas E Burgin Parkway, is a Red Line stop and also serves three MBTA Commuter Rail lines: Kingston, Greenbush and Fall River/New Bedford. From the station it is a short walk along Hancock Street to Kilroy Square and the parade route. For a bigger train day, Edaville in Carver runs a Holiday Express through its light displays, and the Old Colony and Fall River Railroad Museum in Fall River has more than 240 feet of model track on select dates.

kidfact: America's first railroad ran through Quincy. In 1826 horses pulled carts of granite along the Granite Railway, and that stone went to build the Bunker Hill Monument.
faq: When is the Quincy Christmas Parade?

The City of Quincy holds its Christmas Parade at noon on the Sunday after Thanksgiving. It starts at Hancock Street and Walter J. Hannon Parkway and travels up Hancock Street to North Quincy High School, with floats, marching bands and costumed characters, and Santa rides at the end. The 2025 parade was the city's 72nd.
Where does Santa land in Quincy?

Santa and his elves arrive by helicopter at Pageant Field, 1 Merrymount Parkway, at noon on the Saturday of Thanksgiving weekend. The City of Quincy invites families to meet a favorite holiday character while they wait for the Jolly Old Elf to touch down, so arrive a little early for a good view of the field.
Is there free ice skating in Quincy at Christmas?

Yes. The Patriot Ledger lists the opening of a free outdoor skating rink in Quincy Center among the city's holiday events, right after Santa's helicopter arrival and the Christmas Parade. Outdoor skating depends on the weather, so check the City of Quincy's website for the current hours before you bring the skates.
Which train station is closest to Quincy's Christmas events?

Quincy Center station on the Red Line, at 175 Thomas E Burgin Parkway, is a short walk from Hancock Street and Kilroy Square. Kingston, Greenbush and Fall River/New Bedford Commuter Rail trains stop there too. The MBTA has posted parade day detours that move Quincy Center buses to Quincy Adams, so the train is the easier choice.
Why is Quincy linked to America's first railroad?

The Granite Railway, chartered in 1826, carried granite from quarries in West Quincy through East Milton to the Neponset River. The Milton Historical Society notes it was the first railway in the country to operate under a charter, to incorporate and to begin operations, and its stone was used for the Bunker Hill Monument.
